topic: Iterations per row (1 process start per image, single-shot rows 4; 1 warm-up + 3 measured or the harness equivalent)
text: JMH rows (37 FULL rows): -f 0 -wi 1 -w L -i 3 -r L, L per row (rowclass.tsv, c100_repro_protocol.md §11): 0.2 s for 22 rows, 0.5 s for 9 rows (re2j, jackson, lucene-jmh, flexmark, mustache, commons-text, commonmark, jsqlparser, opennlp), 1 s for 5 rows (commons-csv, rhino, snakeyaml-engine, pdfbox, snakeyaml); java-json-benchmark keeps its own CLI setting (-wi 1 -i 3 -m 1: one 10-s JMH-default warm-up + 3 measured 1-s iterations; Cli.java has no -w/-r and -m takes whole seconds). Uniform rows (json-parser, biojava, jsoup, regex-redux, luindex, dacapo-pmd, dacapo-lusearch, dacapo-graphchi, dacapo-batik, dacapo-avrora, dacapo-xalan, dacapo-zxing, dacapo-h2, dacapo-fop, dacapo-sunflow): UW=1 warm-up + UM=3 measured iterations. guava: Hunt3Port args "1 3" (C100 "1 2"), one value per start (best of 3). Single-shot rows (owasp, palantir, antlr, commons-codec): one timed pass per process, 4 starts per image = 32 points per config. Fixed-harness rows (csv-parsers-comparison, gson, handlebars, lucene-bytask, minimal-json): the harness's own in-process warm-up/measurement, one value per start; these rows and guava have 8 points per config (P = I); lucene-bytask uses the 2-round .alg hunt3-indexLineFile-enwiki-r2.alg (C100 r3 minus its third round; round 0 warm-up, round 1 = time key addDoc s r1). The per-row protocol is in the "protocol per start" column.

Row value R = equal-weight geomean over the row's time keys (sub-benchmarks) of the ratio of geometric means cfg/BASE, all 8 images per config pooled equally, alignment and build ignored (time-normalised: thrpt keys inverted; > 1 = slower). Equivalently R = exp(mean s_cfg - mean s_BASE) with point score s = mean_k log x_k. 95 % CI on the log scale: exp(D +- t_{0.975, Welch-Satterthwaite df} * SE), SE = sqrt(v_cfg/n_cfg + v_BASE/n_BASE). Two variants of a data point, shown side by side: (P) per process START (score = mean of that start's measured iterations; JMH/uniform 8 per config, single-shot 32, fixed-harness 8) and (I) per measured ITERATION (JMH/uniform 24 per config; single-shot and fixed-harness identical to P). Warm-up iterations are excluded in both. R is identical in P and I (every start has the same number of iterations); only the CI, n and df differ. Significance is left to the reader: the "CI excludes 1.00" flag is given per variant. Source: welch-summ.py -> welch-report.tsv; method note docs/archive/research/c101_pooled_stat.md.

Class columns per variant = latest/c100/gen_latest.py classify() (the C99 rules incl. the JMH exception) with t = R, the variant's Welch CI as the time interval and the C100 allocation inputs (alloc A, else CUR, else time only for JMH/port rows, else whole-process; jmh flag = "JMH"/"port" in the C100 harness column). The generator re-runs classify on the 4-decimal report values and checks it against welch-report.tsv (0 mismatches).

Allocation was not re-measured in C101 (it does not depend on code alignment). alloc A (per-op / per-key, the paper aggregation), CUR and whole-process are copied unchanged from the C100 tables (latest/c100/full.csv, perrep_*.csv); see latest/c100/README.md for their provenance (C100 final campaign).

Columns A32..A256 = data/<source slot>.tsv of the kit (align-summ.py): per alignment a, the geomean over keys of mean(cfg_a)/mean(BASE_a), 2 builds each, cfg compared only with the BASE of the same alignment. Shown for information; they enter neither R nor the CI.
